currentContext.business: The Company manufactures and retails jewellery made from gold, diamond, platinum, silver and other precious and semi-precious stones under the 'Senco Gold & Diamonds' brand, and retails lifestyle products - lab-grown diamond jewellery, premium leather accessories and fine fragrances - through its wholly owned subsidiary Sennes Fashion Limited. Distribution combines 102 Company-Owned (COCO) showrooms, 85 franchise-operated showrooms (79 FOFO and 6 FOCO), 12 Sennes lifestyle stores and 2 Dubai showrooms with digital touchpoints such as the MySenco app, DigiGold, DigiSilver and Sencoverse. Its customer base spans value-driven mass buyers to aspirational and premium segments across metros and tier-2, tier-3 and tier-4-and-below towns, with particularly strong traction among wedding shoppers and younger, design-conscious consumers; in-house manufacturing through Senco Gold Artisanship Pvt. Ltd. caters to about 7-8% of total sales.

Jewellery (core): Gold jewellery (22K, 18K, 14K and 9K, including lightweight and lower-caratage)
Polki, precious and semi-precious stone jewellery
Digital / phygital platforms: 'Shape of You' AI jewellery personalisation app

currentContext.strategies: Calibrated showroom expansion weighted towards franchise showrooms, in line with an explicitly asset-light strategy, after adding 26 showrooms net in FY26 to reach 201|Premiumisation of the product portfolio through the studded and diamond range, which the CFO credits with catalysing the growth journey|Broaden the entry-price and everyday-wear range through lightweight and lower-caratage jewellery across 22K, 18K, 14K and 9K, including the FY26 launch of 9-karat jewellery|Deepen the 'Phy-gital' omni-channel model across online, offline and B2B channels through DigiGold, Magic Mirror and Sencoverse, with the old gold exchange programme as a key affordability enabler|Diversify beyond gold through Sennes (lab-grown diamonds, premium leather accessories and fragrances), with management expecting lab-grown diamonds to become a dominant part of the Indian market within five years|Improve inventory productivity under a 'SMART' framework - Strategic Stocking, Merchandise Monitoring, Assortment Optimisation, Replenishment Excellence and Technology-Driven Inventory|Optimise borrowing cost by increasing the proportion of Gold Metal Loans in the borrowing mix, after the GML share fell from 67% to 33% in FY26|Strengthen subsidiary performance (SGAPL, SGJTL, SFL) and the performance of showrooms in newer geographies|Geographic diversification from the eastern-India base into a pan-India footprint while retaining market leadership in the east; Bengal and East India remain the stated engine for future growth|Ethical sourcing and brand equity reinforcement, cited via the IAGES accreditation, alongside prudent hedging and disciplined inventory management|Technology and AI deployment across the enterprise - 'Shape of You' personalisation, AI-powered customer engagement bots, location performance intelligence and AI-driven auto stock shuffling|Unified HR policies across subsidiaries, leadership development (RAPID programme) and franchise HR standardisation via the Zing platform across 25+ franchisee locations|This bundle carries no statement of dividend, reinvestment or balance-sheet philosophy. The only capital-allocation item present is the 32nd AGM agenda, which asks members to confirm the interim dividend already paid and to declare a final dividend for the year ended March 31, 2026; the Dividend Distribution Policy that governs it sits in the Board's Report, which was not routed to this domain.|Energy: use of energy-efficient lighting and air-conditioning, monitoring of electricity consumption to reduce wastage, and active evaluation of low-carbon transport and renewable energy sources - stated as the mitigation for the GHG/energy material issue. No quantified emission or renewable-energy target is disclosed in this bundle.|Water: conservation through low-flow fixtures, monitoring of water use to reduce wastage, and rainwater harvesting implemented at selected locations. No quantified water target is disclosed in this bundle.|Responsible sourcing (identified as an opportunity, not a risk): materials sourced from environmentally and socially responsible suppliers, use of recycled gold to conserve foreign exchange and reduce the environmental and social impacts of mining, with the supplier base for ethical and responsible sourcing being increased through third-party certifications and audits.|Governance: Board-level oversight on critical matters supported by regular training and robust audit and review mechanisms, identified as an ethical-governance opportunity; a Risk Management Committee constituted per statutory requirement performs risk assessment and minimisation, with the Board periodically reviewing the framework and a Risk Management Policy published on the website.|Human rights / workplace: Whistle-Blower and Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) policies with designated committees; two POSH cases were filed during FY 2025-26 and zero remained pending at year end. Employee sentiment is tracked through 'Amber', an AI-enabled employee feedback platform.|Diversity: 3 of 7 Board members are women (42.86%), 0 of 3 Key Management Personnel are women, and 1 of 7 Senior Management Personnel is a woman (14.29%); 18 differently-abled employees and 2 differently-abled workers are employed, and the Company reports four employees from the LGBTQ community.|Stakeholder grievance redressal: documented mechanisms and published weblinks for communities, investors, shareholders, employees and workers, customers and value chain partners; 2,375 customer complaints were filed in FY 2025-26 with 25 pending at year end (2,879 filed and 26 pending in FY 2024-25), and 2 shareholder complaints filed with none pending.|CSR: applicable under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013; a Board-level CSR Committee oversees the CSR framework and recommends the annual action plan under a published CSR Policy.|Value chain partners: karigars, vendors and hallmarking centres are routed through their respective merchandisers for grievance resolution; no awareness programmes for value chain partners were conducted during the year (the BRSR leadership-indicator table is filled with dashes).
currentContext.expansion: Expansion at Senco is retail-footprint led rather than plant led. During FY26 the Company launched 26 showrooms (net addition of 26, after closing 2 COCO stores to improve capital efficiency), taking the network to 201 showrooms comprising 102 Company-Owned (COCO) stores, 85 franchise-operated stores (79 FOFO and 6 FOCO), 12 Sennes lifestyle stores and 2 international showrooms in Dubai operated through Senco Global Jewellery Trading LLC. Presence was extended into Rajasthan and Maharashtra through franchise models, with new geographies including Bikaner, Nagpur and Etawah, alongside a continued focus on Bengal and East India. Six of the additions were COCO stores, and the MD&A attributes part of the increase in borrowings to funding those 6 new COCO stores together with an inventory build-up of Rs 19,968 million ahead of the festive season and the West Bengal assembly elections; total borrowings rose from Rs 17,678.90 million in FY25 to Rs 23,452.60 million in FY26. Manufacturing capacity is provided by a dedicated in-house facility under Senco Gold Artisanship Pvt. Ltd., where local karigars handcraft designs; this facility caters to about 7-8% of total sales, and no installed capacity in physical units is disclosed. Investments in subsidiaries increased by Rs 100.00 million to Rs 414.84 million, entirely on account of capital infusions into Sennes Fashion Limited, and management states that the subsidiaries - especially SFL and SGJTL - will require sustained funding for future growth. The Company also began operating 20 Melorra franchise stores during the year, on which business support service expenses of Rs 200.2 million were incurred against nil in the previous year. Inventory days stand at ~183 days against a management target of 160-170 days, which the Company plans to close through AI-driven forecasting and smarter inter-store stock reallocation in FY27. Forward expansion intent, as stated in the outlook, is calibrated showroom expansion with an elevated roll-out of franchise showrooms in line with an asset-light strategy; no showroom-count target or rupee capex plan for FY27 is given in this bundle.
currentContext.mdna: Elevated and volatile gold prices are expected to persist amid global uncertainties; domestic gold prices rose ~79% YoY in FY26 to a peak of Rs 1,69,403 per 10 grams, expanding sales value even as physical gold volumes moderated by ~6%|Recent changes in the customs duty structure on gold imports may influence demand in the short term|Structural demand drivers described as firmly intact: jewellery's cultural, emotional and investment value, weddings and festivals, rising disposable incomes and a young demographic|India's wedding industry is estimated at over Rs 10 lakh crore, with jewellery accounting for 25-35% of total wedding spend|The Indian jewellery market is valued at ~US$ 90 billion and is expected to scale to US$ 130 billion by FY30, with the organised:unorganised split at 40:60 and the organised share expected to keep gaining|Formalisation tailwind from mandatory hallmarking, GST compliance and anti-money-laundering norms shifting share to organised, branded players - described as a multi-year structural tailwind|Elevated prices are expected to sustain the mix shift towards lightweight, lower-caratage, silver and studded jewellery|Old gold exchange remains a key affordability enabler - 44% of total FY26 sales and ~50% of Q4 revenue|Same Store Sales Growth of ~24% for FY26 (~35% in Q4) evidences the existing-showroom contribution to growth alongside new stores|Margin levers cited: premiumisation and favourable product mix (reported gross margin 13.5% to 19.8%; adjusted gross margin 16.2%), against which management flags that excluding one-time gold-price gains the underlying EBITDA margin is ~8.5%|Working capital intensity is structural: inventory rose 61% on gold prices, new showrooms and festive build-up, taking blended inventory holding to 186 days and leaving operating cash flow negative at Rs 7,893 million|Financing cost driver: the GML share of borrowings fell from 67% to 33% because of margin-call-related liquidity pressure in volatile Q3/Q4, lifting the blended borrowing cost by 100 bps to 6.9%|Emerging categories - lab-grown diamond alternatives and 9K/14K lightweight gold - are opening new product and consumer categories|Management cautions on the evolving competitive landscape, elevated gold prices and global geopolitical uncertainties

risks.risk: Margin risk - profitability heavily reliant on the gold jewellery segment
risks.note: The Company states that profitability and margins are heavily reliant on the gold jewellery segment, so any supply disruption during gold procurement or adverse movement in market prices is a material financial risk. Gold jewellery accounted for ~85% of total revenue in FY26. Mitigation is product diversification into diamond, polki and platinum, and new verticals in leather accessories and lab-grown diamonds.

risks.risk: Macroeconomic risk to discretionary consumer spending
risks.note: Geopolitical tensions, supply chain disruptions, elevated inflation, global monetary tightening and a broader slowdown threaten to limit discretionary spending, a direct risk to growth of the gems and jewellery industry. Mitigation cited is a strong domestic core, retail and e-commerce expansion, portfolio innovation and a broader geographic footprint so no single territory's cycle dominates.

risks.risk: Competition risk from organised and unorganised players
risks.note: The sector is characterised by intense competition from both organised and unorganised participants; failure to consistently deliver high-aesthetic, premium-quality products at competitive price points would directly threaten market share, revenue stability and long-term growth. Mitigation is brand equity, design portfolio depth, product innovation and brand amplification.

risks.risk: Data security and privacy / data-protection compliance
risks.note: The Company flags that data privacy infringement would materially affect the business and any breach could lead to non-compliance with data privacy law. Mitigation is cloud-based storage, software upgrades and continuous system hardening in line with new data privacy laws; ITGC audits are conducted by the internal auditors to mitigate cyber fraud and error risk.

risks.risk: GHG emissions and energy management (BRSR material issue, classified a risk)
risks.note: Purchased electricity in jewellery manufacturing and retail outlets raises Scope 2 emissions, and transportation and supply-chain activity raises Scope 3; the Company notes lab-grown diamonds are carbon intensive and will affect Scope 3 emissions in the long term. Stated financial implication is negative - it increases operational cost. Mitigation is energy-efficient lighting and air-conditioning, electricity monitoring, and evaluation of low-carbon transport and renewable energy.

risks.risk: Water stewardship (BRSR material issue, classified a risk)
risks.note: Water usage in offices and manufacturing is identified as a significant risk given potential water scarcity from climate-related water stress; stated financial implication is negative. Mitigation is low-flow fixtures, monitoring of water use and rainwater harvesting at selected locations.

BRSR Section A reports 100% of turnover from one main activity - manufacturing and retailing of jewellery with lifestyle and fashion accessories - across 18 States and 1 Union Territory, with exports contributing only 5% of total turnover and international presence limited to a single country. Earnings are therefore concentrated in one product category and one domestic market.

BRSR turnover rate for permanent employees rose to 27.00% in FY 2025-26 from 24.20% in FY 2024-25 and 19.00% in FY 2023-24 (female attrition 32.00% in FY26), a structural retention pressure in a showroom-led, service-intensive retail model; permanent worker turnover by contrast is 1.00%.

one-line thesis: Senco Gold delivered a record FY26 with 33% revenue growth driven by 60% gold price appreciation and a strategic pivot to old gold exchange (50% of Q4 sales), though management guides conservative 18-20% growth for FY27 citing volume pressure from high prices and competitive margin compression despite operating leverage.
financial scorecard: Revenue INR 1,997cr (+45% YoY Q4), INR 8,430cr (+33% YoY FY26); EBITDA INR 274cr (13.7% margin Q4, +116% YoY), 11.5% FY26 (inflated by ~2.5-3% price rise gains); PAT INR 157cr (+151% YoY Q4); Order Book N/A (Retail); Net Debt increased due to 61% inventory build to INR 5,296cr (186 days) driven by price hikes and festival stockpiling; One-offs include customs duty revision inventory gains recognized over 2 quarters.
guidance: Revenue growth 18-20% (conservative base case, internal target higher); EBITDA margin 7.5-7.8% (sustainable normalised vs 11.5% reported); Store additions 18-20 net new stores; Capex focused on franchise expansion in Tier 2/3/4.
order book & pipeline: N/A for retail model; Sales momentum strong in April (+67% Akshaya Tritiya/Poila Boishakh), moderated in late May due to PM's gold exchange appeal and Adhik Maas.
segment / subsidiary detail: Jewellery constitutes 94% of sales (Coin/Bullion only 6%); Diamond value growth +32%, volume +9%; Old gold exchange contributed ~50% of Q4 revenue and ~44% of FY26 revenue; 9/14/18 carat gold mix ~13-15% of total sales.
growth verticals / optionality: Geographic diversification beyond East India (currently 50-60% focus) to North/Central India (30-40% focus); Franchise model scalability in Tier 3/4 towns; Sennes brand (lab-grown diamonds/lifestyle) now EBITDA positive with 12 exclusive stores; Increasing own manufacturing from 5% to 10% long-term.
margins & cost dynamics: Reported FY26 EBITDA 11.5% vs guided sustainable 7.5-7.8%; ~2.5-3% margin boost from gold price appreciation/inventory gains; Competitive intensity limits operating leverage expansion to 10-15 bps; Marketing spend steady at 1.8-2.2% of revenue.
capex / expansion: Store expansion capex via franchise-heavy model to reduce capital intensity; Working capital intensity high due to inventory build (INR 5,296cr); GML utilization targeted >50% to lower borrowing costs (currently 3-3.5% vs higher bank rates).
capital allocation: Final dividend 20% proposed (plus 15% interim); Reinvestment in store network and brand building (Sennes); Debt reduction secondary to working capital needs for inventory.
risks & watch-items: Gold price volatility impacting consumer volume demand; Intense competition from national players entering East India and local unorganised discounting; Regulatory changes on gold imports/customs duties; Execution risk in non-East India markets.
management quality / tone: Optimistic on long-term structural growth but prudently conservative on guidance; Emphasizes sustainability via old gold exchange and affordability (lightweight/lower carat); Acknowledges short-term demand softness in late May but expects recovery post-monsoon/wedding season.
non-obvious takeaways: Old gold exchange strategy aligns with government import reduction goals, creating a structural moat and ESG narrative; Inventory gains from customs duty hikes will flow through P&L over next 2 quarters, smoothing earnings; Sennes brand reached EBITDA profitability faster than expected (Year 2).
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| High gold prices driving consumers to exchange old gold rather than buy new; Senco's 50% exchange mix captures this flow better than peers with lower exchange penetration. | Senco Gold Ltd | beneficiary | High | Company explicitly guided 50-55% exchange mix as new normal, directly benefiting from PM's push to reduce gold imports and recycle household gold. |
| Competitors like Titan operating at 11-12% margins vs Senco's 7.5-7.8% due to lower diamond mix; Senco's push into diamonds and Sennes may take time to close gap. | Senco Gold Ltd | loser | Med | Margin convergence with industry leaders is a multi-year journey; near-term margins capped by competitive pricing in new geographies. |

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures and retails jewellery made from gold, diamond, platinum, silver and other precious and semi-precious stones under the 'Senco Gold & Diamonds' brand, and retails lifestyle products - lab-grown diamond jewellery, premium leather accessories and fine fragrances - through its wholly owned subsidiary Sennes Fashion Limited. Distribution combines 102 Company-Owned (COCO) showrooms, 85 franchise-operated showrooms (79 FOFO and 6 FOCO), 12 Sennes lifestyle stores and 2 Dubai showrooms with digital touchpoints such as the MySenco app, DigiGold, DigiSilver and Sencoverse. Its customer base spans value-driven mass buyers to aspirational and premium segments across metros and tier-2, tier-3 and tier-4-and-below towns, with particularly strong traction among wedding shoppers and younger, design-conscious consumers; in-house manufacturing through Senco Gold Artisanship Pvt. Ltd. caters to about 7-8% of total sales.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Senco Gold Artisanship Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary, 100% held, incorporated/acquired 14-10-2020, reporting currency INR; in-house jewellery manufacturing arm. Counterparty for purchases of inventory, job-work charges, procurement advances, rental income and support-services income.
- Senco Global Jewellery Trading LLC, UAE — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary, 100% held, incorporated/acquired 14-02-2023, reporting currency AED; Dubai-based B2C and B2B jewellery trading. Counterparty for sales of inventory, expenses incurred on its behalf and support-services income.
- Sennes Fashion Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary, 100% held, incorporated 07-09-2024, reporting currency INR; lifestyle retail. Counterparty for equity infusions, inventory purchases and sales, asset purchase, rent paid and rental income.
- Jai Hanuman Shri Siddhivinayak Trust — related party: Entity having control over the Company; dividend transactions recorded during the year.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Jewellery constitutes 94% of sales (Coin/Bullion only 6%); Diamond value growth +32%, volume +9%; Old gold exchange contributed ~50% of Q4 revenue and ~44% of FY26 revenue; 9/14/18 carat gold mix ~13-15% of total sales.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Jewellery (core):** Gold jewellery (22K, 18K, 14K and 9K, including lightweight and lower-caratage), Diamond jewellery, Platinum jewellery, Silver jewellery and products, Polki, precious and semi-precious stone jewellery, Gold coins, Customised jewellery design services

certifications.title: Quality certifications
certifications.body:

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: N/A for retail model; Sales momentum strong in April (+67% Akshaya Tritiya/Poila Boishakh), moderated in late May due to PM's gold exchange appeal and Adhik Maas.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue growth 18-20% (conservative base case, internal target higher); EBITDA margin 7.5-7.8% (sustainable normalised vs 11.5% reported); Store additions 18-20 net new stores; Capex focused on franchise expansion in Tier 2/3/4.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Geographic diversification beyond East India (currently 50-60% focus) to North/Central India (30-40% focus); Franchise model scalability in Tier 3/4 towns; Sennes brand (lab-grown diamonds/lifestyle) now EBITDA positive with 12 exclusive stores; Increasing own manufacturing from 5% to 10% long-term.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Elevated and volatile gold prices are expected to persist amid global uncertainties; domestic gold prices rose ~79% YoY in FY26 to a peak of Rs 1,69,403 per 10 grams, expanding sales value even as physical gold volumes moderated by ~6%
- Recent changes in the customs duty structure on gold imports may influence demand in the short term
- Structural demand drivers described as firmly intact: jewellery's cultural, emotional and investment value, weddings and festivals, rising disposable incomes and a young demographic
- India's wedding industry is estimated at over Rs 10 lakh crore, with jewellery accounting for 25-35% of total wedding spend
- The Indian jewellery market is valued at ~US$ 90 billion and is expected to scale to US$ 130 billion by FY30, with the organised:unorganised split at 40:60 and the organised share expected to keep gaining
- Formalisation tailwind from mandatory hallmarking, GST compliance and anti-money-laundering norms shifting share to organised, branded players - described as a multi-year structural tailwind
- Elevated prices are expected to sustain the mix shift towards lightweight, lower-caratage, silver and studded jewellery
- Old gold exchange remains a key affordability enabler - 44% of total FY26 sales and ~50% of Q4 revenue
- Same Store Sales Growth of ~24% for FY26 (~35% in Q4) evidences the existing-showroom contribution to growth alongside new stores
- Margin levers cited: premiumisation and favourable product mix (reported gross margin 13.5% to 19.8%; adjusted gross margin 16.2%), against which management flags that excluding one-time gold-price gains the underlying EBITDA margin is ~8.5%
- Working capital intensity is structural: inventory rose 61% on gold prices, new showrooms and festive build-up, taking blended inventory holding to 186 days and leaving operating cash flow negative at Rs 7,893 million
- Financing cost driver: the GML share of borrowings fell from 67% to 33% because of margin-call-related liquidity pressure in volatile Q3/Q4, lifting the blended borrowing cost by 100 bps to 6.9%
- Emerging categories - lab-grown diamond alternatives and 9K/14K lightweight gold - are opening new product and consumer categories
- Management cautions on the evolving competitive landscape, elevated gold prices and global geopolitical uncertainties

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Reported FY26 EBITDA 11.5% vs guided sustainable 7.5-7.8%; ~2.5-3% margin boost from gold price appreciation/inventory gains; Competitive intensity limits operating leverage expansion to 10-15 bps; Marketing spend steady at 1.8-2.2% of revenue.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Final dividend 20% proposed (plus 15% interim); Reinvestment in store network and brand building (Sennes); Debt reduction secondary to working capital needs for inventory.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Expansion at Senco is retail-footprint led rather than plant led. During FY26 the Company launched 26 showrooms (net addition of 26, after closing 2 COCO stores to improve capital efficiency), taking the network to 201 showrooms comprising 102 Company-Owned (COCO) stores, 85 franchise-operated stores (79 FOFO and 6 FOCO), 12 Sennes lifestyle stores and 2 international showrooms in Dubai operated through Senco Global Jewellery Trading LLC. Presence was extended into Rajasthan and Maharashtra through franchise models, with new geographies including Bikaner, Nagpur and Etawah, alongside a continued focus on Bengal and East India. Six of the additions were COCO stores, and the MD&A attributes part of the increase in borrowings to funding those 6 new COCO stores together with an inventory build-up of Rs 19,968 million ahead of the festive season and the West Bengal assembly elections; total borrowings rose from Rs 17,678.90 million in FY25 to Rs 23,452.60 million in FY26. Manufacturing capacity is provided by a dedicated in-house facility under Senco Gold Artisanship Pvt. Ltd., where local karigars handcraft designs; this facility caters to about 7-8% of total sales, and no installed capacity in physical units is disclosed. Investments in subsidiaries increased by Rs 100.00 million to Rs 414.84 million, entirely on account of capital infusions into Sennes Fashion Limited, and management states that the subsidiaries - especially SFL and SGJTL - will require sustained funding for future growth. The Company also began operating 20 Melorra franchise stores during the year, on which business support service expenses of Rs 200.2 million were incurred against nil in the previous year. Inventory days stand at ~183 days against a management target of 160-170 days, which the Company plans to close through AI-driven forecasting and smarter inter-store stock reallocation in FY27. Forward expansion intent, as stated in the outlook, is calibrated showroom expansion with an elevated roll-out of franchise showrooms in line with an asset-light strategy; no showroom-count target or rupee capex plan for FY27 is given in this bundle.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Optimistic on long-term structural growth but prudently conservative on guidance; Emphasizes sustainability via old gold exchange and affordability (lightweight/lower carat); Acknowledges short-term demand softness in late May but expects recovery post-monsoon/wedding season.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- 87+ year heritage brand built on craftsmanship, integrity and customer-centricity, with a family lineage running from 1938 in Dhaka to a fourth-generation entrepreneur as MD & CEO
- Retail scale and density: 201 showrooms across 18 States and 1 UT plus Dubai, with stated market leadership in eastern India by number of stores
- Asset-light franchise model (79 FOFO and 6 FOCO stores) allowing expansion into new regions with optimal capital allocation alongside 102 owned stores
- Design catalogue depth: 218K gold jewellery designs and 122K diamond jewellery designs, with new designs released every month
- In-house manufacturing arm (SGAPL) plus a network of 277-plus master karigars, giving control over craftsmanship and quality
- Old gold exchange programme accounted for 44% of total FY26 sales, sustaining footfall and affordability at elevated gold prices
- Phy-gital / omni-channel reach: MySenco app (1.02 lakh downloads), DigiGold, DigiSilver, Sencoverse and Magic Mirror alongside physical showrooms
- Customer jewellery purchase schemes approved by the Registrar of Companies, with over 1,00,000 customers enrolled in the new 'Swarna Saubhagya' scheme and an average upsell of 10% at redemption, providing customer-led cash inflows
- Credit rating upgraded to CARE A+ during the year
- Quality and trust controls: gold purity and diamond carat testing, testing of old gold in front of customers, 100% hallmarking, multi-stage QC backed by lifelong buy-back
- Diversification optionality through Sennes (lab-grown diamonds, leather accessories, fragrances) and the Dubai subsidiary

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Gold price volatility impacting consumer volume demand; Intense competition from national players entering East India and local unorganised discounting; Regulatory changes on gold imports/customs duties; Execution risk in non-East India markets.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Old gold exchange strategy aligns with government import reduction goals, creating a structural moat and ESG narrative; Inventory gains from customs duty hikes will flow through P&L over next 2 quarters, smoothing earnings; Sennes brand reached EBITDA profitability faster than expected (Year 2).

challenges.body:

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Hedging policy] A detailed gold-price risk framework: daily rate fixing of old gold, trading jewellery and GML "for the equivalent amount of gold sold ... ensures that there is no cash loss or business losses"; sales hedging at 90%-110% daily/weekly and inventory hedging at "~50% of gold inventory value as per board policy"; instruments are unfixed GML (~10% to ~40% of gold inventory, which "acts as a hedging instrument") and MCX Futures & Options sell positions (~10% to ~40%).
- [Hedge accounting] "Senco's hedge accounting is aligned with Ind AS 109 (IFRS 9)"; effective-hedge impact is "adjusted to inventory valuation through WACC method, thus impacting Gross Margin" while ineffective-hedge impact goes to other income/expenses. "Since Senco does not apply Cash Flow Hedge accounting, any reference to OCI or deferred recognition of hedge ineffectiveness is not applicable".
- [Customs duty] Management describes a customs-duty rise "from 6% to 15%" that caused demand contraction, and separately says "Indian gold prices are post-custom duty increase impact of 9%" with "The benefit of the custom duty rise ... likely to accrue over Q3, net of the impact of price fall due to the hedging level"; a footnote separately flags "one time adverse impact of custom duty reduction in FY25 which had been adjusted to Inventory and Gross Margin".
- [Labour code] "We have also considered full impact of Labour code in Q1 after detailed evaluation."
- [Subsidiary performance] "Business losses at SFL and SGJTL also affected consolidated profitability, while SGAPL continued to report profit" — SFL "is still in the growth phase and incurred losses" while the Dubai entity SGJTL "incurred losses due to extraordinary market situation in gulf based on gulf war and Hormuz imbroglio".
- [Regulatory environment] Sector regulation cited as mandatory hallmarking with HUID marking (mandatory from 2021, HUID mandatory from 2023), "Mandatory Hallmarking for 9 Carat Gold from July 2025", mandatory PAN for transactions over Rs 2,00,000, and Anti Money Laundering applicability with "CBIC designated as a regulator for the jewellery industry".
- [Industry sizing — deck contradicts itself] The strategy slide states "India's jewellery TAM: $90 Bn (FY25) → $130 Bn (FY30E), organised share rising 40% → 50%", while the industry section is titled "India's Gems and Jewellery Market likely to Scale to TAM of $ 162 Billion" and carries the figures 162, 106 and 115 (USD Bn) against FY25/FY26/FY30E. Both readings are recorded; they are not reconciled in the deck.
- [Market structure] India is described as "The 2nd Largest Jewellery Consuming Nation" at 26% of global consumption versus China 28%, "the 2nd largest gold market in the world", with 70% share of gold jewellery out of total gold demand, rural India at 60% of demand versus urban 40%, and gold jewellery falling from 84% (FY24) to 83% (FY29E) of the Indian market while studded rises 12% → 13%. West Bengal and Maharashtra each hold 17% of BIS-registered hallmarked gold jewellery retailers.
- [Technology stack] Eight-element digital framework listed as ERP driven organization, ISO Certification, Modern Digital Platforms, Centralized Network Management System, AI-Driven Customer Service, Data Driven Decision Making, 360° CRM platform and AI-Driven Martech, supporting an omnichannel "Phygital" hub-and-spoke fulfilment model.
